extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers, study section chairs, and scientists who participate in NIH study section review
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating the content, purpose, and potential biases of the Chair's summary in NIH study section peer review; guidance for reviewers and chairs about what a proper Chair summary should (and should not) do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on major strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair summary should "focus the panel's attention on the set of major strengths and weaknesses."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summaries should highlight the principal strengths and weaknesses that drove discussion and scoring, keeping attention on the most important evaluative points rather than secondary details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview the score-driving comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair summary should "overview the score driving comments."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary should explicitly surface the comments or reasons that are driving the score distribution, making clear which critiques or praises were decisive for the panel's judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note areas of consensus and disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair summary should "note areas of consensus and disagreement."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summaries must reflect where the panel was aligned and where opinions diverged, so voting members understand the nature and extent of any disagreement rather than presenting a falsely unified view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not substitute for panel members' active engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chair summary should not substitute for panel members' active engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Chair's recap is a supplement, not a replacement, for each reviewer having listened to the discussion and forming their own judgment; it should not be used by members to avoid engaging with the discussed evidence and arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid creating a recency effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of the 'recency effect' where the summary occurs immediately before voting and can shift scores via timing and the Chair's subjective interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chairs should structure summaries to minimize undue influence caused by timing (e.g., ensure summaries do not introduce new emphases at the last moment); reviewers should be cautious of changing scores solely based on a fresh recap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurately represent what was discussed (avoid discrepancies with reality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summaries should not "emphasize written critiques that never came up in discussion, or mischaracterize where the panel actually landed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chairs must ensure the recap matches the actual verbal discussion and votes; mischaracterizations are an anti-pattern that can mislead voters and distort panel record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize authority influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that "Chairs hold field standing, which carries persuasive weight regardless of intent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chairs should avoid letting their status substitute for argument — summaries should be neutral and fact-based to reduce undue deference. Reviewers should be aware of potential authority bias when hearing the Chair's words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for systemic constraints on chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the structural pressures: "Chairs are time-pressured and managing many responsibilities; this is structural."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate summaries with awareness of possible omissions or simplifications caused by workload and time constraints; institutional fixes (e.g., more time, support) may be needed to improve summary quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Should not shepherd votes into conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: Question whether the Chair summary serves any legitimate function "beyond shepherding the vote into line and promoting conformity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high-quality summary should inform deliberation without pressuring members to conform. Watch for language or framing that appears intended primarily to align votes rather than clarify issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers should weigh scores against the panel discussion, not the chair-summary recap
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are advised to "weigh their own scores against the panel discussion, not the chair-summary recap."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual reviewers should prioritize the substance of the full panel discussion and their independent assessments when casting votes, using the Chair summary only as a supplementary recap, not as the primary basis for changing scores.
